chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Iblees says to his army, 'Cast envy and transgression between them, for both of these equate to Shirk in the presence of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: Why are envy and transgression considered equivalent to Shirk in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reveals the strategic priority of Satan, who instructs his legions to sow envy (*al-hasad*) and transgression (*al-bagh*) among humanity. This highlights a profound Shia theological insight: while Shirk is the ultimate sin, the subtle corruption of social bonds and individual excesses are deemed equally weighty in divine judgment, serving as effective precursors to major disbelief.
